archetypes.name: design-flow
archetypes.rationale: The diff rewires /design Gate B, Step 3.6, and validator escalation, so a state-machine specialist can catch bad routing interactions beyond the static panel.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the /design control-flow changes around default auto-apply, --approve explicit mode, Step 3.6 assessor routing, and transitions back to Step 3b. Check that every branch has a clear settled state, preserves Gate C behavior, and does not accidentally bypass size brakes or validator handling. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: autofix-launch
archetypes.rationale: The new plan-command auto-fix helper integrates external Codex/Cursor launchers, validation, timing, and prompt rendering across multiple call sites.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the cross-vendor auto-fix helper and its SKILL.md integration with the shared validator failure path. Focus on launcher argv, workspace/add-dir boundaries, revalidation semantics, retry caps, status parsing, and whether all caller sites resume the right surrounding success or escalation path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: revert-state
archetypes.rationale: The assessor Revert option mutates plan snapshots, review counters, and round artifacts, which needs specialized state-restoration review.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate snapshot-plan-round revert behavior and the Step 3.6 Revert branch. Check that plan.txt, plan-after-round files, plan-review artifacts, review-round-count.txt, plan-review-round-cursor.txt, and assessor artifacts remain mutually consistent for round 1, later rounds, and failure fallback. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: trust-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The diff sends validator logs and plan files to external agents and changes redaction/evidence handling, creating a focused trust-boundary surface.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate trust-boundary handling for validator logs, plan-file content, prompt construction, redaction fallback, and external agent workspaces. Check whether untrusted plan or validator output can become executable instructions, leak secrets, or cause edits outside the intended design tmpdir. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: runtime-compat
archetypes.rationale: The diff lowers Python requirements and CI versions from 3.12 to 3.11 across several surfaces, which may affect runtime assumptions and docs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the Python 3.11 compatibility change across CI, lint/type-check config, bootstrap checks, docs, and Python package metadata. Look for remaining 3.12 assumptions, dependency incompatibilities, or mismatched user-facing prerequisite claims. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
